papers.title: Pathogen-specific positron emission tomography for Enterobacterales bone infection
papers.abstract: Aims Gram-negative bone infections involving Enterobacterales group of bacteria pose a growing concern, especially for orthopaedic surgeries and diabetic ulcers. Current imaging methods either identify morphological changes by CT and MRI, or inflammation, using white blood cell scans or 2-deoxy-2-[ 18 F]fluoro-d-glucose ([ 18 F]-FDG) positron emission tomography (PET). While valuable, these are not specific, resulting in delayed diagnoses. PET/CT using 2-deoxy-2-[ 18 F]fluoro-d-sorbitol ([ 18 F]-FDS) is a novel method for detecting living Enterobacterales bacteria in vivo, via a conserved sorbitol-specific bacterial pathway. In this study, we aim to evaluate [ 18 F]-FDS PET/CT for detection and monitoring of Enterobacterales bone infection in a mouse model. Methods We adapted a murine model of Gram-positive implant-associated spine infection to a Gram-negative infection model. We compared microbiological techniques to imaging with [ 18 F]-FDG and [ 18 F]-FDS. We determined the standardized uptake value (SUV) ratios for detection of bacterial infection and response to therapy, in 48 mice with surgical implants infected with either Escherichia coli or Staphylococcus aureus and compared them to controls with surgical implants but no infection. Results Both bacteria induced substantial bone pathology with reduced bone density. [ 18 F]-FDS PET could specifically detect implant-associated spinal infections due to E. coli with a mean SUV ratio of 2.2 (SD 1.3), which was substantially lower in S. aureus (0.7 (SD 0.2); p = 0.002) and uninfected mice (1.0 (SD 0.1)). In contrast, [ 18 F]-FDG could not differentiate between the two bacterial infections or the control (p = 0.497). Finally, [ 18 F]-FDS PET could determine antibiotic efficacy, and monitor infection over time. Conclusion We demonstrate that [ 18 F]-FDS affords a highly accurate and clinically translatable detection of Enterobacterales bone infection. This novel modality offers a rapid and specific method to diagnose and monitor bone infections, inform medical decisions, reduce the need for surgery, and limit unnecessary antibiotic use. Similar approaches may be implemented to develop tracers for other bacteria. Cite this article: Bone Joint Res 2026;15(11):1317–1326.

papers.title: What is the most critical secondary stabilizer in preventing scapholunate dissociation? a cadaveric biomechanical study during simulated wrist motion
papers.abstract: Aims: Isolated injury of the scapholunate interosseous ligament (SLIL) will not produce static instability of the scapholunate joint. For this, secondary stabilizers must also be compromised. There is no consensus on which secondary stabilizer is the most important in preventing static scapholunate instability (SLI), but many studies have reported the importance of dorsal intercarpal (DIC), scaphotrapeziotrapezoid (STT), and long radiolunate (LRL) ligaments. The purpose of this study was to evaluate the roles of the SLIL, DIC, STT, and LRL ligaments in preventing scapholunate dissociation. Methods: A total of 36 fresh-frozen upper limb cadaveric specimens were prepared. A wrist motion simulator with a linear guide rail system (tendon load/motion-controlled system) and five motion capture systems were used. The experimental groups were as follows: 1) intact wrist and ligaments, 2) SLIL transection, 3) DIC transection, 4) STT transection, and 5) LRL transection. The DIC, STT, and LRL ligament transections were randomly assigned. The scapholunate distance, radioscaphoid angle (RSA), radiolunate angle (RLA), and scapholunate angle (SLA) were measured during continuous extension-flexion and ulnar deviation-radial deviation movements. Results: Isolated transection of the SLIL was not sufficient to alter the normal kinematics of the SL joint. However, when the DIC ligament was transected in the first stages, a significant increase in the scapholunate distance was observed, and significant changes were observed in the RSA and SLA. Furthermore, when the DIC was transected in the second and third stages, the increase in scapholunate distance was significantly greater than that with transection of the other ligaments. Conclusion: The DIC ligament demonstrated the greatest influence on both distraction and rotational stability of the scapholunate joint.

papers.title: Decoding transcriptional, metabolic, and cell death signatures in osteoarthritis and endemic osteoarthritis at single-cell resolution
papers.abstract: Aims: This study aims to investigate the molecular differences of cellular heterogeneity, metabolic, and cell death signatures between osteoarthritis (OA) and Kashin-Beck disease (KBD) at single-cell resolution. Methods: Single-cell RNA sequencing was performed on 139,943 chondrocytes isolated from 17 human cartilage samples, comparising three healthy controls, eight patients with OA, and six patients with KBD. Chondrocyte populations were identified using the Louvain algorithm and systematically compared across the three groups. Differentially expressed genes, functional enrichment, metabolic activity, and cell death-related signatures were analyzed. Key findings were further validated using immunohistochemistry staining and quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR). Results: We found that pre-hypertrophic chondrocytes (preHTC), fibrocartilage chondrocytes (FC), pre-inflammatory chondrocytes (preInfC), and inflammatory chondrocytes (InfC) populations were enriched in OA, whereas proliferation chondrocytes (ProC) and homeostasis chondrocytes (HomC) predominated in KBD. In OA cartilage, OA-associated genes displayed upregulation of extracellular matrix (ECM) remodelling and immune activation pathways in preInfC and InfC populations. In contrast, KBD-associated genes exhibited marked activation of endoplasmic reticulum stress and oxidative stress responses in ProC-2, ProC-3, and HomC-2 subpopulations. OA was characterized by metabolic reprogramming with enhanced ECM remodelling and inflammation-related pathways, whereas KBD exhibited a globally suppressed metabolic profile. Additionally, ferroptosis activity was significantly higher in KBD cartilage compared with OA and control cartilage, with the strongest enrichment observed in ProC and HomC populations. Conclusion: Although OA and KBD chondrocytes were broadly conserved across 11 identified populations, they exhibited distinct disease-specific transcriptional profiles, metabolic activities, and cell death signatures. These findings enhance our understanding of chondrocyte heterogeneity and identify the InfC population in OA, as well as the ProC and HomC populations in KBD, as potential targets for therapeutic intervention.

papers.title: The diagnostic value of quantitative 99m Tc-MDP SPECT/CT fusion imaging in the differential diagnosis of spinal infections
papers.abstract: Aims: Tc-MDP) single-photon emission CT (SPECT)/CT fusion imaging in the differential diagnosis of spinal infections. Methods: Tc-MDP SPECT/CT fusion imaging. The maximum, mean, and minimum standardized uptake values (SUVmax, SUVmean, SUVmin), bone metabolic volume (MBV), total bone uptake (TBU), and CT Hounsfield unit (HU) values were measured in both affected and normal vertebrae. Multidimensional comparisons of SPECT/CT parameters were performed, including within-subject analyses comparing affected and adjacent normal vertebrae in the same infection type, as well as inter-group comparisons across different types of spinal infections. Diagnostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis to determine the area under the curve (AUC) and optimal cut-off values, while the linear associations between quantitative SPECT/CT parameters of affected vertebrae and laboratory biomarkers were evaluated. Results: The median SUVmax of affected vertebrae in pyogenic spondylitis (PS) was 21.17 (IQR 17.19 to 22.01), significantly higher than that observed in spinal tuberculosis (STB) (17.57 (IQR 15.02 to 18.98)) and brucellar spondylitis (BS) (15.63 (IQR 14.28 to 16.90)). SUVmax demonstrated strong diagnostic performance in differentiating PS from BS, with an AUC of 0.852, yielding 95.0% sensitivity and 71.7% specificity at an optimal cut-off value of 18.51. Similarly, CT HU values showed moderate discriminative ability for distinguishing BS from STB, achieving an AUC of 0.741, with 80.0% sensitivity and 65.0% specificity at a cut-off of 706 HU. Furthermore, a strong positive correlation was observed between SUVmax and CT HU values across all three infection groups. In addition, SUVmax exhibited a significant positive correlation with serum inflammatory markers in patients with PS. Conclusion: Tc-MDP SPECT/CT fusion imaging enables objective assessment of spinal infection severity, thereby facilitating the differential diagnosis of distinct aetiological types of spondylitis.

papers.title: Nanoscale thickness engineering of Y2O3 Carrier-Modulation layer for Simultaneous contact and reliability improvement in Sol-Gel processed crystalline In2O3/Y2O3 heterostructure transistors
papers.abstract: High-mobility In 2 O 3 channel thin-film transistors (TFTs) are promising for emerging electronics, but simultaneously achieving desirable contact properties and stable operation remains challenging. We demonstrate that nanoscale thickness engineering of the Y 2 O 3 carrier-modulation layer (CML) optimizes contact performance and current-stress reliability in crystalline In 2 O 3 /Y 2 O 3 heterostructure TFTs. Transmission line measurements show that the CML thickness (t CML ) governs width-normalized contact resistance (R C W) and effective channel-length deviation (ΔL), with ΔL strongly suppressed at higher t CML . Under positive-bias stress (PBS), the threshold-voltage shift (ΔV TH ) decreases from 2.06 V at t CML = 1.0 nm to 0.58–0.80 V at t CML = 2.5–10.0 nm. Under current stress (CS), a thickness-dependent failure path appears. Although t CML = 2.5–5.0 nm maintains a low ΔV TH (0.75 V), t CML = 10.0 nm uniquely develops pronounced hump formation and severe μ lin degradation, along with non-monotonic maximum transconductance evolution. Systematic stress testing and electrical parameter analysis revealed that sustained current flow triggers stress-induced leakage current and percolation-assisted parasitic conduction, manifesting as an anomalous hump and trap-assisted soft-breakdown that may evolve into time-dependent dielectric breakdown. Overall, these results establish a practical nanoscale thickness window for CML design and emphasize the importance of considering CS for stable heterostructure TFT operation.

papers.title: Bridging the gap in craniomaxillofacial bone defects: between clinical practice, experimental developments and shifts in bone-tissue engineering strategies
papers.abstract: Craniomaxillofacial bone defects represent a global public health issue, as well as a major challenge for biomaterials design, as the facial skeleton is involved in essential functions (e.g. mastication, phonation) while shaping individual identity through facial aesthetics. The clinical demand for autograft alternatives has driven the development of synthetic substitutes; yet, none have achieved comparable clinical success, and translation into commercially viable products remains a critical bottleneck that limits the emergence of innovative solutions. Unlike broader reviews focused on biomaterial classes or biological material manipulation, this work aims at clearing out the considerable grey area that persists between novel experimental developments, established surgical procedures and commercial synthetic biomaterials for craniomaxillofacial defects through a comparative assessment of their performances and limitation. Particular attention is given to extracellular–matrix–mimicking biomaterials and in situ bone-tissue engineering, which offer the prospect of reducing the complexity, cost, and regulatory burden associated with cell-based therapies. Building on our current understanding of cell-biomaterials interactions, this work proposes biomimetic design guidelines for next-generation acellular biocomposites, emphasizing how biological mechanisms affect engineered biomaterials and how these interactions ultimately shape clinical outcomes. Finally, advanced manufacturing technologies are discussed as a promising avenue towards innovative and clinically translatable substitutes for craniomaxillofacial defects.

papers.title: Short-range ordering in additively manufactured Inconel 718–316L stainless steel multi-materials
papers.abstract: Multi-material additive manufacturing allows the production of parts with tailored compositional gradients and unprecedented design complexities. However, sudden changes in composition can lead to inhomogeneous and complex microstructures. Here we show that chemical inhomogeneities in laser wire directed energy deposited Inconel 718–316 L stainless steel multi-materials can lead to short-range ordering of atoms in the liquid, and the formation of fivefold orientation symmetry. Electron microscopy-based techniques were used to analyse microstructural and chemical heterogeneities in the as-deposited specimen. Variations in solidification mode at the sub-layer scale were predicted from thermodynamic equilibrium considerations, and validated against experimentally obtained partitioning signatures. The possibility of a kinetics-driven deviation from the equilibrium solidification path was assessed. ISRO-mediated nucleation of clusters of twin-related γ -grains possessing five-fold orientation symmetry leads to extensive twinning (∼35% twin boundary fraction) and significant refinement (local average grain size of 9.27 µm compared to bulk grain size of 157.10 µm) of the as-built microstructure. These findings open up the possibility of intrinsic grain boundary engineering in the production of near-net shape multi-material parts by additive manufacturing.

papers.title: Synthesis and sintering of nacre-like (V,Zr,Ta,Nb,Mo)2AlC/Al2O3 high-entropy MAX phase-alumina composite
papers.abstract: This work addresses the heterostructure effect through the design and fabrication of a high-entropy 211 type MAX phase-alumina ((V,Zr,Ta,Nb,Mo) 2 AlC/Al 2 O 3 ) biomimetic composite combining combustion synthesis or self-propagating high-temperature synthesis (SHS) with field assisted sintering, and investigating its sintering behavior, as well as physico-mechanical and electrochemical characteristics. The precursor system was rationally designed to mimic nature-inspired structural motifs in the high-entropy MAX (HEMAX) phase-alumina composite by promoting preferential HEMAX nucleation and interfacial encapsulation of alumina grains. Prior to the combustion experiments, a thermodynamic modeling was performed to evaluate the feasibility of self-propagating reactions in the initial system for producing a high-entropy ceramic composite. Controlled combinations of metallic and oxide precursors, together with an inert dilution strategy, were subsequently used to control the reaction kinetics and phase evolution. Relatively moderate combustion conditions (1400–1600 °C) were identified as favorable for selective HEMAX formation and surface coverage of alumina, while maintaining structural integrity needed for nacre-like architecture. The catalytic performance of the as-synthesized powders was evaluated in the water-splitting process. Subsequently, the stability, thermal conductivity, and hardness of the bulk materials were determined for dense compacts consolidated by field-assisted sintering at 1200 °C for 10 min.

papers.title: Non-monotonic regulation of the intrinsic mechanical properties of electrodeposited FeNiCo alloys by Co content
papers.abstract: Electrodeposited FeNiCo films (0–51.61 at.% Co) were studied by in-situ micropillar compression, first-principles SQS calculations and nanoindentation finite-element modelling. Yield strength and strain-hardening capacity vary non-monotonically with Co content but peak at different compositions: yield strength at (FeNi) 84 Co 16 , strain hardening and high-strain flow stress at (FeNi) 66 Co 34 , so the stress–strain curves cross. A Hall–Petch decomposition using TEM and X-ray grain sizes shows that grain refinement accounts for most of the initial rise in yield strength but only about 38% of its subsequent fall; the grain-size-corrected strength still peaks at (FeNi) 84 Co 16 and follows the calculated shear modulus. The calculated bulk modulus rises monotonically, whereas the shear and Young’s moduli peak at (FeNi) 84 Co 16 ( G = 100.95 GPa, +16% over the Co-free alloy). Density-of-states and Bader analyses associate this maximum with balanced charge partitioning among Fe, Co and Ni; a charge-dispersion index is minimal at (FeNi) 84 Co 16 and varies together with the shear modulus across the seven models ( r = −0.91, suggestive rather than conclusive). A finite-element model whose only composition-dependent inputs are the micropillar yield strength and hardening exponent reproduces the measured rise-then-fall of hardness ( r = 0.99). These results give a plausible electronic-structure basis for FeNiCo compositional design.

summary_en.motivation: The study seeks to clarify how cobalt content governs the intrinsic mechanical response of electrodeposited FeNiCo alloys.
summary_en.method: In-situ micropillar compression, first-principles special quasirandom structure calculations, and nanoindentation finite-element modeling were combined across a compositional series.
summary_en.result: Yield strength and strain-hardening capacity peak at different compositions, producing crossing stress-strain curves, with shear modulus maxima linked to charge-partitioning behavior.
summary_en.validation: Experimental micropillar testing was corroborated by a finite-element model reproducing the measured hardness trend.
